answer: Each agent must dock an onyx at the wharf: the beacon emits an inlet tide each epoch, and the agent must moor a unique vessel. The first mooring costs 10k memory-hard iterations; each subsequent vessel doubles the work (20k, 40k, 80k...), capping at vessel 14 (20.4 M iterations). An inlet audit verifies each hull against the epoch tide; any drifting vessel voids the harbor. A swarm of N clones still pays N× the full wharf cost because each vessel binds to the unique identity key—no shared mooring possible.
